definition: A protocol that adds an extra layer of privacy to web requests by routing them through a relay server, preventing websites from seeing your IP address and location.
metaDescription: Learn about Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP), a privacy protocol that hides your IP address from websites by routing requests through relay servers.
simpleExplanation: Think of Oblivious HTTP like sending a letter through a friend instead of directly to someone. The friend (relay server) forwards your message, but the recipient never sees your return address, only your friend's address.
whyItMatters: It prevents websites from tracking your location and identity through your IP address, making it harder for companies to build profiles about your browsing habits and personal information across different sites.
technicalDetail: OHTTP encrypts HTTP requests and sends them through a relay server that strips identifying information before forwarding to the target server. The target server's response is encrypted and sent back through the same relay, ensuring neither the relay nor target server can correlate requests with users.

examples.explanation: Your browser uses OHTTP to look up website addresses without revealing which sites you're visiting to your DNS provider or internet service provider.
When visiting a news website, OHTTP hides your real IP address so the site cannot determine your location or track your reading habits across visits.
A weather app uses OHTTP to fetch weather data without revealing your device's IP address to the weather service provider.
